newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S 1997 AGRICULTURAL OUTPUT SEEN UP 1.5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S 1997 AGRICULTURAL OUTPUT SEEN UP 1.5 PCT.

text.p: Poland's agricultural output is likely to grow by 1.5 percent in 1997, after a 0.3-percent growth in 1996, Government Centre for Strategic Studies (CSS) said in a report on Wednesday.
It said crop output was likely to stay flat, after a 2.3-percent growth in 1996, but livestock output could rise by 3.5 percent, after a 2.4-percent fall last year.
CSS said winter sowings were badly damaged, but the good weather conditions and increased summer sowings would help the final 1997 crop output.
It said stabilisation of grains prices, low potatoe prices, accompanied by rising livestock prices, made livestock breeding attractive.
